items.title: One of Ontario’s top Italian festivals brings a taste of Italy to Mississauga
items.summary: Mississauga is about to get a taste of Italy as one of the city’s biggest and longest-running cultural celebrations returns to Celebration Square this weekend. Mississauga Italfest is expected to draw large crowds to the city centre on Friday and Saturday as thousands of people gather for two days of Italian food, music, traditions and entertainment. The free festival runs Friday, Aug. m. m. and Saturday, Aug. m. at Mississauga Celebration Square. Now in its 15th year, Italfest has grown from a local celebration into one of Ontario’s Top 100 Festivals, attracting visitors from across the province, Canada, the United States and even Italy. The annual event was founded in 2012 by a group of Canadian Italians looking to preserve and share Italian traditions. It has since become a major fixture on Mississauga’s summer festival calendar. And there will be plenty to see, hear and eat this weekend. Visitors can expect authentic Italian food, fresh pasta and pizza, espresso and cannoli, food trucks, artisan vendors and more than 60 vendors and artisans throughout the festival. Music and entertainment will take over the Celebration Square stages, with international performers, Italian folk acts, heritage dancers, regional choirs and Canadian music veteran Alfie Zappacosta among the featured performers.

items.title: Big winter event being planned now in Mississauga
items.summary: The city is looking for people and groups who want to participate in what’s expected to be a “signature winter experience” for years to come in Mississauga’s downtown core. Some nine months removed from what the City of Mississauga described as a “highly successful” 2025 Christmastime spectacle, in which the annual Santa Claus parade returned to Mississauga’s City Centre by Square One for the first time in almost 25 years, officials are now ramping up efforts to organize this year’s major event. The 2026 Santa Claus parade is scheduled for Saturday, Nov. 21 in the downtown core and the city is putting out the call for float entries and walking groups who want to participate. m. The annual parade, this year being presented under the theme “Sauga’s Home for the Holidays,” will kick off the holiday season, “bringing together dazzling, illuminated floats, festive entertainment and family-friendly fun,” city officials said this week. Parade and other activities part of the plan The lighting of the Christmas tree at Celebration Square and the opening for the season of Mississauga’s largest outdoor ice rink, also at the square, are also taking place the afternoon and evening of the parade. The 2026 parade theme invites participants to showcase the “traditions, cultures, stories and people that make our city feel like home,” the city said, adding “organizations interested in participating are encouraged to apply early. ” Applications that meet participant criteria will be reviewed on a first-come, first-served basis and will close on Sept. 30 or once the parade hits capacity, officials noted.

items.title: Regional Chair Iannicca Leads Push for Infrastructure and Housing Funding at Ontario Municipal Conference
items.summary: According to INsauga, Peel Region officials used this week's Association of Municipalities of Ontario conference to press the provincial government for more support on infrastructure, housing, healthcare and other essential services as Mississauga, Brampton and Caledon continue to grow. INsauga reports Regional Chair Nando Iannicca, along with members of regional council and senior staff, met with provincial ministers, parliamentary assistants and ministry officials to discuss the region's priorities. One of the region's top priorities, according to INsauga, was securing long-term infrastructure funding to keep pace with growth and offset pressures tied to development charges. In a meeting with the Ministry of Infrastructure, Peel officials pushed for provincial funding to support growth-related projects and the infrastructure needed for new housing and economic development, and INsauga reports the province and Peel committed to continuing that work together. Housing was another major focus of the region's discussions, this time with the Ministry of Municipal Affairs and Housing, where officials raised housing affordability, homelessness and the need to expand the supply of affordable housing while strengthening the municipal-provincial partnership, according to INsauga.

items.title: EllisDon Announces Strategic Facilities Management Partnership with Scotiabank Arena
items.summary: This content may have been approved or produced by a partner Mississauga, ON, Aug. 20, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) — EllisDon Facilities Services (EDFS) is pleased to announce a new facilities management partnership with Scotiabank Arena , supporting the ongoing operation and performance of one of Canada’s most recognized sports and entertainment venues. Mississauga, ON, Aug. 20, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) — EllisDon Facilities Services (EDFS) is pleased to announce a new facilities management partnership with Scotiabank Arena , supporting the ongoing operation and performance of one of Canada’s most recognized sports and entertainment venues. Under the agreement, EDFS will provide Building Operations Management Maintenance Services (BOMMS) to Scotiabank Arena along with other properties under the organization’s portfolio including, Real Sports Bar & Grill , e11even Restaurant, and Ford Performance Centre. The scope of services includes the supervision, maintenance, repair and inspection of critical building systems, including mechanical, electrical, building automation, and fire and life safety systems that support the professional sports and entertainment operations. EDFS will oversee preventative maintenance programs, asset planning, energy management, and continuous improvement initiatives designed to support the reliabilityand long-term performance of these facilities. “We’re excited to partner with EllisDon to further strengthen the operational support behind Scotiabank Arena as we combining their technical expertise with our knowledge of our existing teams,” said Elis Valera, Vice President of Venue Operations & General Manager, Scotiabank Arena. ” The partnership represents a significant milestone for EllisDon as it continues to expand its footprint across complex, high-performance environments.

items.title: Twin 16-Storey Towers Now Proposed for Dundas Street Plaza Redevelopment, Down From 18 Storeys
items.summary: According to INsauga, a proposal to redevelop a plaza at 1225 Dundas Street East, just west of Dixie Road, has been revised again as it heads back for review next month. INsauga reports the site currently houses several businesses, including Danforth Food Market, Baituna Furniture and Spoon and Fork. The project has changed shape more than once since developers first applied in 2022 for a 12-storey apartment building with 462 units, ground-floor retail and 34 townhouses. By 2024, according to INsauga, the plan had grown to an 18-storey terraced building with two point towers connected by a shared nine-storey podium. The latest version submitted to the City of Mississauga scales that back to two 16-storey apartment buildings connected by a six-storey podium, INsauga reports, with developers Stephen-Mitchell Reality Limited, Whitehorn Investments Limited, Lynrob Investments Limited, Richco Investments Limited and Tobdele Investments Limited behind the application.

items.title: 1930 Meadowvale Village Bridge Gets Restoration Work as Wider Road Study Continues
items.summary: According to INsauga, Peel Region has closed one lane of the Old Derry Road bridge in Mississauga's Meadowvale Village area from today through Friday to allow restoration work on the structure. INsauga reports the bridge crosses the Credit River between Historic Trail and Credit Valley Conservation Road, with traffic control measures in place in the area for the next three days. The bridge, built in 1930, is a designated heritage structure within the Meadowvale Village Heritage Conservation District and serves as a scenic gateway into the historic community, according to INsauga. The restoration work comes as the City of Mississauga carries out a broader environmental assessment study for Old Derry Road, launched earlier this year, INsauga notes. That study is considering improvements including pavement rehabilitation, new cycling infrastructure and the repair or replacement of existing bridge structures along the road, including the Old Derry Road bridge itself.

items.title: ‘Everything I love and care about is right here’: In her push to regain the mayor’s seat Bonnie Crombie promises tax relief and a prosperous future for Mississauga
items.summary: When Bonnie Crombie departed the mayor’s chair in 2024, she told The Pointer she wakes up each morning thinking of her constituents, with one thought on her mind. ” “That will always be forefront in my mind,” she said. Entering the fray for what is shaping up to be the most contentious mayoral race Mississauga has seen in decades, at a pivotal point in the municipality’s history, that mindset is guiding her early campaign messaging. In a wide-ranging interview, Crombie explained that if elected to the post she previously held for almost a decade, she will take a hard look at City spending, with plans to bring in an outside auditor to review every line of Mississauga’s budget. The balancing act, she explains, is utilizing taxpayer dollars effectively; investing to build the city of the future, while avoiding the type of cuts that only cripple residents down the road. There are plenty of savings that can be found in between, for the taxpayer, she vows. ” With a growing infrastructure gap, massive proposals for downtown growth, and a ballooning police budget that no politician in Peel has been willing to stand up against, the vision Crombie has for Mississauga will require balancing what the municipality realistically requires of its taxpayers and the politically popular path many elected officials take when trying to get elected, promising cuts that simply are not realistic.
